title: Raising awareness of strength training for middle-aged and older Singaporeans
asked: Ms Mariam Jaafar asked what the Ministry is doing to raise awareness of strength training and resistance activity among middle-aged and older Singaporeans, and what plans exist to support safe, guided strength training for those who lack confidence or knowledge to use gym equipment.
response: Ms Rahayu Mahzam said HPB and SportSG jointly issue the Singapore Physical Activity Guidelines, which recommend muscle-strengthening activities at least twice a week, and run outreach, gym orientation workshops and community programmes such as Start2Move. She said functional outcomes are tracked for some of the more structured programmes, but the details were not with her. For gyms, she said ActiveSG gyms have onsite trainers and introductory programmes for people unfamiliar with equipment. On the request for an ActiveSG facility in the Admiralty part of Woodlands, she said the North's needs are being looked at and she does not want to pre-empt the written PQ answer.

key_points.point: The Singapore Physical Activity Guidelines recommend muscle-strengthening activity at least twice a week.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: recommend that adults engage in muscle-strengthening activities at least twice per week

key_points.point: The Ministry is exploring gym orientation workshops to familiarise seniors with gym equipment.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: exploring organising gym orientation workshops to familiarise seniors with gym equipment

key_points.point: Start2Move is a beginner-friendly community programme with a guided introduction to strength-building exercises.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: Start2Move, a beginner-friendly programme with guided introduction to strength-building exercises in a supportive environment

key_points.point: Expanded community nodes plus the Healthy 365 app are the channels for reaching seniors.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: With this expansion, plus the Healthy 365 app, we can better reach out to seniors and engage them in strength training exercises.

key_points.point: Functional outcomes are tracked for some of the more structured programmes.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: we do for some of the more structured programmes

key_points.point: ActiveSG gyms have onsite trainers willing to support users of the equipment.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: For the ActiveSG gyms, there are trainers who are onsite, who are very willing to support and encourage those who come and attend to use the equipment.

key_points.point: On the request for an ActiveSG facility in Admiralty, the North's needs are being looked at and the written PQ answer is not being pre-empted.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: I do not want to pre-empt the answer to the written PQ, but we can definitely look into this.

key_points.point: The Healthy 365 app is offered as a starting point for residents seeking guidance.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: the Healthy 365 app does provide a very good starting point

left_open: The detailed functional outcome data for participants in the structured programmes

Whether an ActiveSG facility will be provided in the Admiralty part of Woodlands
supplementary: Whether programmes reach less active people in their 40s and 50s, how their functional outcomes are tracked, and gym access and venues.
